destination.title: Multifield inflation: backgrounds, perturbations and effective descriptions
destination.question: How do additional fields and field-space geometry change inflationary dynamics, observable perturbations and the validity of effective descriptions?
destination.summary: Assisted inflation, matrix models, turning trajectories, perturbation transfer and effective theories form a useful broad family. Single-field baselines, alternative matter and gravitational interactions, numerical methods and late-time acceleration provide qualified connections.

systems: Multiple scalar fields, including matrix-valued and effective quantum-moment descriptions
Scalar–gauge systems and scalar-dependent curvature couplings as extensions
Single-field and antisymmetric-tensor models as comparisons or alternate homes
targets: Inflationary mechanisms, trajectories, attractors and endings
Primordial perturbations, entropy transfer and effective-theory control
Conditional field-range and quantum-gravity consistency questions
regimes: Ordinary slow roll, assisted scaling, constant roll and sustained or transient turning, kept distinct
Late-time acceleration only through explicit application links
assumptions: No universal requirement of negative field-space curvature, light potential-Hessian modes or Swampland criteria
Model-specific assumptions remain local to their source questions
Ordinary and pre-Swampland work remains eligible
conventions: Field-space dimension and spacetime dimension are separate
Potential and Hubble slow-roll parameters are not universally interchangeable
Background stability, entropy-variable growth and observable species isocurvature are distinct
Constituent excursions, trajectory length and geodesic separation are not interchangeable
includes: Distinct mechanisms and methods linked by inflationary questions
Source-scoped questions whose canonical equivalence remains untested
excludes: Treating numerical membership as scientific equivalence
Treating moduli stabilization, generic adaptive-mesh software or dark-energy models as demonstrated inflationary mechanisms
Inferring observational viability or ultraviolet completion from background existence alone

sources.title: Weak Gravity Conjecture for the Effective Field Theories with N Species

evidence.text: How does a large number N of field sectors change a gravity-compatible effective theory's ultraviolet cutoff, and can the resulting theory support assisted slow-roll inflation?

sources.title: M-flation: Inflation From Matrix Valued Scalar Fields

evidence.text: Can three matrix-valued scalar fields support inflation with small effective couplings and large collective field excursions, while their remaining degrees of freedom supply distinctive perturbations and preheating?

sources.title: Matrix Inflation and the Landscape of its Potential

evidence.text: Which classical inflationary sectors arise from matrix-valued inflatons, how can quantum transitions connect their vacua, and what curvature, entropy and tensor spectra occur in selected two-field examples?

sources.title: Hyperbolic Inflation

evidence.text: Can negative field-space curvature sustain centrifugal inflation without ordinary slow roll, produce suitable primordial perturbations and remain radiatively stable?

sources.title: What does inflation say about dark energy given the swampland conjectures?

evidence.text: Can curved multifield inflation relax the single-field connection between scalar tilt, potential curvature and tensor amplitude, thereby admitting larger swampland parameters?

sources.title: Shift-symmetric orbital inflation: Single field or multifield?

evidence.text: Can inflation with sustained turning and an unstabilized, exactly massless isocurvature direction produce nearly adiabatic, Gaussian observables resembling single-field inflation despite strongly multifield dynamics?

sources.title: Hyperinflation generalised: from its attractor mechanism to its tension with the ‘swampland conditions’

evidence.text: How does field-space geometry change inflationary motion and fluctuation masses? A small curvature radius L permits rapid trajectory turning and can induce instabilities transverse to otherwise slow-roll motion.

sources.title: Rapid-Turn Inflationary Attractors

evidence.text: Does a similarly general rapid-turn construction and perturbation reduction exist for more than two scalar fields?

sources.title: Multi-field inflation from single-field models

evidence.text: Can independent quantum moments turn a minimally coupled, single-field Higgs-like inflation model into an observationally viable effective multifield model, with non-adiabatic dynamics preparing slow roll and ending inflation?

sources.title: Generalizing the swampland: Embedding $P(X, \varphi)$ inflationary theories in a curved multifield space

evidence.text: This setting describes noncanonical single-field inflation whose background and perturbations a proposed two-field extension must reproduce.

sources.title: On the choice of entropy variables in multifield inflation

evidence.text: Which entropy variables consistently describe multifield inflation in curved field space, permit matching through reheating to observable species isocurvature, and distinguish physical destabilisation from apparent growth caused by the chosen variable?

sources.title: Inflation with strongly non-geodesic motion: theoretical motivations and observational imprints

evidence.text: How does strongly non-geodesic inflation arise in negatively curved field space, how does it permit inflation on Planck-steep potentials, and what naturalness limitations and primordial observational signatures accompany it?

sources.title: (Slow-)twisting inflationary attractors

evidence.text: When do multifield inflationary trajectories approach stable late-time attractors, how do field-space isometries and torsion constrain them, and can three-or-more-field backgrounds and perturbations exhibit behavior beyond the two-field case?

sources.title: Cosmological perturbation theory with trinity of scalar fields

evidence.text: How can explicit three-field curvature/isocurvature equations be formulated for arbitrary flat-field-space potentials, how do trajectory turns affect their spectra, and what can radiation-era correlations reveal about inflationary degrees of freedom?

sources.title: Adiabatic and entropy perturbations from inflation

evidence.text: How do adiabatic and entropy perturbations evolve and become correlated in multiple-field inflation, and when can entropy perturbations change the large-scale curvature perturbation during inflation or preheating?

sources.title: An Observational test of two-field inflation

evidence.text: Does two-field slow-roll inflation retain an observable tensor–scalar consistency condition after model-dependent super-horizon evolution and reheating, and can late-time correlations reconstruct the curvature spectrum at horizon exit?

sources.title: Hybrid inflation

evidence.text: Can coupled scalar fields produce inflationary regimes and endings beyond gradual slow rollover and first-order bubble transitions? The paper develops a rapid waterfall model and Brans–Dicke hybrids with curvature-induced or slow-roll symmetry breaking.

sources.title: Dynamics of assisted inflation

evidence.text: Why is the assisted-inflation scaling trajectory an attractor for many exponential-potential fields, and what homogeneous, adiabatic, and isocurvature perturbations arise near it without a slow-roll approximation?

sources.title: Scalar perturbations during multiple field slow-roll inflation

evidence.text: How can scalar matter and gravitational perturbations be calculated accurately to first order in slow roll for arbitrarily many fields with nonminimal kinetic terms, including horizon crossing, trajectory rotation and entropy sourcing?

sources.title: Weak Gravity Conjecture for the Effective Field Theories with N Species

evidence.text: Divide S < EL by E and insert the relativistic gas ratio S/E. This produces the lower size bound needed to test compatibility with the independently derived collapse upper bound.

sources.title: M-flation: Inflation From Matrix Valued Scalar Fields

evidence.text: Use gauge-invariant linear perturbations, first-order slow-roll Hankel solutions and numerical mode evolution. Particle production is estimated with Bogoliubov coefficients and WKB; quartic preheating applies imported elliptic-function and resonance analyses.

sources.title: Matrix Inflation and the Landscape of its Potential

evidence.text: Discuss inter-vacuum transitions through Euclidean-action/WKB paths. For the Case III exit estimate, approximate the potential by a triangle, use ΓCD=M⁴exp(−SE) with M² approximated by false-vacuum V″, and compare Γ/H⁴ with the critical value 9/(4π).

sources.title: Hyperbolic Inflation

evidence.text: In a fixed-de-Sitter, fixed-slope approximation, expand around the orbital background to quadratic order in radial/angular perturbations, Fourier transform, and numerically integrate the coupled mode equations through horizon crossing. The velocity-dependent Coriolis coupling is essential.

sources.title: What does inflation say about dark energy given the swampland conjectures?

evidence.text: Transfer a common inequality parameter from one physical sector to another after restricting it with observations. Here inflation constrains c and c', which are then used in a quintessence sector under an assumed common EFT.

sources.title: Shift-symmetric orbital inflation: Single field or multifield?

evidence.text: The δN formalism estimates the curvature spectrum and local bispectrum. A quadratic perturbation action and coupled superhorizon evolution give the general power-spectrum result; agreement with an earlier in-in calculation is reported up to subleading corrections.

sources.title: A geometrical instability for ultra-light fields during inflation?

evidence.text: When does negative field-space curvature produce a physical instability of inflationary isocurvature modes, rather than identify a repulsive background trajectory, and how does the answer differ for heavy and ultra-light spectator fields?

sources.title: Gauss–Bonnet Inflation and the String Swampland

evidence.text: Why do the adopted gradient and excursion conjectures challenge ordinary single-field slow-roll inflation?

sources.title: Optimized numerical evolution of perturbations across sharp background trajectory turns in multifield inflation

evidence.text: Can multifield scalar perturbations be evolved efficiently through sharp background turns caused by potential structure, field-space geometry, or both, while preserving canonical normalization?

sources.title: Hyper-Non-Gaussianities in Inflation with Strongly Nongeodesic Motion

evidence.text: How does strongly nongeodesic inflation in negatively curved field space affect nonlinear curvature perturbations, and can their non-Gaussianities constrain proposed inflationary attractors?

sources.title: Scaling attractors in multi-field inflation

evidence.text: Which background trajectories can attract two-field inflation when field-space geometry competes with the potential gradient? The paper organizes constant-epsilon trajectories as critical points, including gradient flow and motion with a stationary transverse coordinate.

sources.title: Heavy fields, reduced speeds of sound and decoupling during inflation

evidence.text: Can heavy isocurvature fields be integrated out consistently during sustained slow-roll inflation with c_s²≪1, even though a strongly turning background mixes curvature and isocurvature fields?

sources.title: The Multi-Field, Rapid-Turn Inflationary Solution

evidence.text: Given a scalar potential and field-space metric, which regions admit sustained slow-roll, rapid-turn inflation with arbitrarily many fields, and can those regions be identified without evolving every candidate trajectory?

sources.title: Anisotropic hyperbolic inflation

evidence.text: How does a gauge field alter hyperbolic inflation's attractors and slow-roll destabilization, and how can trajectories transition between anisotropic slow-roll and anisotropic hyperbolic regimes?

sources.title: Fat inflatons, large turns and the $\eta$-problem

evidence.text: Can turning multifield trajectories satisfy proposed quantum-gravity restrictions that are difficult for canonical single-field slow roll?

sources.title: A fake instability in string inflation

evidence.text: Does the tachyonic orthogonal entropy mode in Fibre Inflation signal a physical instability, despite a stable single-field background, or does its growth arise from an unsuitable entropy variable?

sources.title: Inflationary perturbations near horizon crossing

evidence.text: When do horizon-crossing formulae fail because scalar perturbations do not reach their usual asymptotic regime, either during a temporary interruption of inflation or for modes leaving shortly before inflation truly ends?

sources.title: Rapid-Turn Inflationary Attractors

evidence.text: Can rapid turning occur without negative field-space curvature? The imported flat model combines radial stabilization with an angular slope and supplies such an example.

sources.title: Attractors, Bifurcations and Curvature in Multi-field Inflation

evidence.text: Can late-time nongeodesic inflationary attractors be described by one effective-potential framework, including their stability and bifurcations, and can stable turning solutions exist without an isometry along the inflationary direction?

sources.title: Assisted inflation

evidence.text: Can multiple scalar fields with individually steep exponential potentials cooperate through cosmic expansion to produce inflation, and what scaling attractor and curvature-perturbation spectrum result when their slopes differ?

sources.title: Draining the Swampland

evidence.text: Which fields contribute to C1 during inflation, and can a retained spectator remain classical and dynamically negligible?

sources.title: The Swampland Spectrum Conjecture in Inflation

evidence.text: How are multifield inflationary paths and their ordinary field excursions defined? Homogeneous fields evolve under a potential with Hubble friction on a curved, positive-definite target space.

sources.title: Features of heavy physics in the CMB power spectrum

evidence.text: When can heavy transverse fields leave observable primordial-spectrum features through sufficiently rapid turns of an inflationary trajectory, while slow roll continues, and when can a single-mode effective theory capture these effects?

sources.title: Rapid-Turn Inflationary Attractors

evidence.text: How can a heavy transverse field participate in inflation? Negative field-space curvature can destabilize ordinary slow roll and support a displaced turning trajectory in the imported minimal-geometry model.

sources.title: Why Does Inflation Look Single Field to Us?

evidence.text: Can selection for long inflationary durations explain why observations reported at publication were compatible with single-field phenomenology despite multifield high-energy constructions?

sources.title: Primordial Black Holes and the String Swampland

evidence.text: The inflationary setting translates restrictions on a scalar potential into restrictions on primordial perturbations through canonical single-field slow-roll relations.

sources.title: Enhancement of superhorizon scale inflationary curvature perturbations

evidence.text: When can single-field inflation amplify comoving curvature perturbations after horizon crossing, and can background integrals diagnose this without assuming slow roll?

sources.title: Scaling attractors in multi-field inflation

evidence.text: Which curved two-field scalar theories admit attracting inflationary trajectories outside slow-roll slow-turn motion, and how are transitions between geodesic and turning motion organized?

sources.title: Formalizing the slow roll approximation in inflation

evidence.text: How can potential-based and Hubble-based slow-roll approximations be defined consistently, extended order by order, and used to describe inflationary dynamics and its endpoint while retaining the necessary attractor conditions?

sources.title: Constraints on the spectral index for the inflation models in string landscape

evidence.text: Can many identical scalar fields permit slow roll when a constituent potential is too steep? On the equal-field assisted trajectory, the Hubble slow-roll parameter is reduced by the number of fields.

sources.title: Hyperinflation generalised: from its attractor mechanism to its tension with the ‘swampland conditions’

evidence.text: Does a three-field evolution reproduce the analytic dependence on transverse speed? The reported numerical example follows the sum π_w1²+π_w2² rather than identifying either component with the two-field transverse velocity.

sources.title: Gauge-flation trajectories in Chromo-Natural Inflation

evidence.text: Which multifield trajectories and parameter choices generate sufficient Chromo-Natural inflation, and under what conditions do its trajectories reproduce Gauge-flation?

sources.title: Multi-field Inflation in High-Slope Potentials

evidence.text: Can strongly turning multi-field trajectories support prolonged, observationally compatible inflation on steep potentials while satisfying the refined de Sitter and distance swampland criteria, in flat or negatively curved field space?

sources.title: Rapid-Turn Inflationary Attractors

evidence.text: Does a common attractor describe sustained two-field inflation with strongly nongeodesic motion across different field-space geometries and potentials? The paper seeks a background construction and a conditional linear stability criterion.

sources.title: The Swampland Spectrum Conjecture in Inflation

evidence.text: Modular j-inflation supplies a curved two-field example for comparing a path in the upper half-plane with its lift to a potential surface. Its potential is modular invariant and its kinetic geometry is hyperbolic.

sources.title: Modular Inflation at Higher Level $N$

evidence.text: How do two-field entropy modes become the matter-isocurvature observables constrained by CMB data, and how does higher-level reheating affect that mapping?

sources.title: A Tip for Landscape Riders: Multi-Field Inflation Can Fulfill the Swampland Distance Conjecture

evidence.text: The setting describes inflation driven by several scalar coordinates whose kinetic terms define a curved field space. Background trajectories and distances depend on this metric, while perturbations probe both its curvature and the potential.

sources.title: Generalizing the swampland: Embedding $P(X, \varphi)$ inflationary theories in a curved multifield space

evidence.text: When does eliminating an original heavy field at the action level agree with integrating out entropic perturbations?

sources.title: New Effects in Multifield Cosmology Coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet Term

evidence.text: How does scalar coupling to the Gauss–Bonnet term modify two-field rapid-turn inflation, its potential slow-roll relations and consistency conditions, and the possibility of phantom-like dark energy?

sources.title: Two-field constant roll inflation

evidence.text: Under what conditions can two scalar fields realize constant-roll inflation, and does the resulting freedom in the potential improve prospects for matching string-inspired models compared with the rigid single-field construction?

sources.title: Eternal Chaotic Inflation is Prohibited by Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Can many identical scalar fields collectively sustain inflation when an individual field would roll too rapidly? Each field contributes to the common Hubble friction, while its potential derivative remains that of its own uncoupled potential.

sources.title: A Statistical Approach to Multifield Inflation: Many-field Perturbations Beyond Slow Roll

evidence.text: How frequently do slow-roll violations, multifield effects and contributions beyond a two-field truncation affect scalar perturbations in a statistical ensemble of six-field inflationary potentials, especially after imposing constraints on the spectral tilt?

sources.title: Gauss–Bonnet Inflation and the String Swampland

evidence.text: Can a scalar-dependent curvature coupling change inflationary observables enough to accommodate a steep potential and a small field excursion?

sources.title: Fat inflatons, large turns and the $\eta$-problem

evidence.text: Does sustained multifield slow-roll inflation require a light potential-Hessian eigenmode, or can turning motion support inflation while every background-field mass exceeds H?

sources.title: Completely dark matter from rapid-turn multifield inflation

evidence.text: Can negatively curved field space sustain inflation on a steep radial potential through angular motion?

sources.title: Hyperinflation generalised: from its attractor mechanism to its tension with the ‘swampland conditions’

evidence.text: Can a nonsymmetric model enter hyperinflation after an initially stable slow-roll phase? Here negative curvature destabilises the transverse direction as the quadratic potential becomes relatively steeper during descent.

destination.title: Consistency, spectra and realizations of six-dimensional gravity
destination.question: Which anomaly, charge, string, geometric and compactification tests constrain specified six-dimensional gravity theories, their spectra and their realizations?
destination.summary: A proposed navigation family with a six-dimensional gravity core and explicitly marked neighboring questions. No original scientific region statement was supplied beyond numerical candidate membership, so this scope is newly authored and requires independent review.

systems: Six-dimensional supergravity, chiefly N=(1,0), with tensor content specified source by source
R-symmetry-gauged theories, localized supersymmetry breaking and the specified (2,0) gravity setting
Related five-dimensional reductions, conformal sectors and discrete-anomaly systems as qualified bridges
targets: Allowed spectra, enumeration, finiteness and bounds
Charge quantization, global anomalies and gauge-group global forms
String realizability and geometric explanations of anomaly conditions
Admissibility and spectra of string probes
Moduli, matter comparisons and compactification consistency
regimes: Tensor-free, one-tensor and multiple-tensor sectors remain distinct
Ordinary and pre-Swampland work remains eligible
Source-specific geometric and nongravitational limits are retained
assumptions: Necessary tests are not presumed sufficient for a quantum-gravity completion
Completeness, probe existence and geometric realization are imposed only where explicitly supported
Failure of a known construction is not by itself a proof of inconsistency
conventions: Preserve charge normalization, global gauge group, quadratic refinement and free-sector subtraction
Preserve source-specific supersymmetry notation and tensor counts
includes: Descriptions and bounded primary excerpts as separately identified evidence

excludes: A single homogeneous physical question for all numerical members
Universal extrapolation of bounds from restricted tensor or gauge sectors
GUT matter parities and eleven-dimensional boundary coupling as core six-dimensional spectrum questions
Assignment of a dimension or physical system to the underspecified sixth-order-trace facet

sources.title: A Bound on 6D N=1 supergravities

evidence.text: Do Green–Schwarz anomaly cancellation and positivity of kinetic terms alone restrict six-dimensional chiral supergravity with one tensor multiplet to finitely many semisimple gauge groups and matter representations, independently of an explicit UV construction?

sources.title: Global aspects of the space of 6D N = 1 supergravities

evidence.text: How strongly do anomaly cancellation and physical gauge kinetic terms constrain the discrete field content of six-dimensional N=1 supergravity with multiple tensor multiplets, and which additional restrictions characterize F-theory realizations?

sources.title: Anomaly constraints and string/F-theory geometry in 6D quantum gravity

evidence.text: How far do anomaly cancellation and physical gauge kinetic terms constrain discrete 6D supergravity data, and can their relation to F-theory geometry establish or obstruct string universality?

sources.title: 6D supergravity without tensor multiplets

evidence.text: Which gauge groups and matter representations satisfy known low-energy consistency conditions for six-dimensional N=1 supergravity without tensor multiplets, focusing on products of SU(N)? Which apparently consistent spectra exceed known string constructions?

sources.title: Swampland Bounds on the Abelian Gauge Sector

evidence.text: Can consistency of strings coupled to tensor fields impose a finite upper bound on independent U(1) gauge factors in six-dimensional N=(1,0) quantum gravity, including theories with non-abelian sectors?

sources.title: On the consistency of a class of R-symmetry gauged 6$D$ $\mathcal{N}$=(1,0) supergravities

evidence.text: Do three locally anomaly-free, R-symmetry gauged six-dimensional supergravities satisfy stronger quantization and global-anomaly criteria, assuming they possess suitably behaved dyonic strings?

sources.title: On the finiteness of 6d supergravity Landscape

evidence.text: Do anomaly cancellation, string-charge consistency, and BPS-string worldsheet unitarity bound the number of massless modes in six-dimensional supergravity with eight supercharges? Can the same probes constrain bulk matter representations beyond anomaly cancellation?

sources.title: Anomalies as obstructions: from dimensional lifts to swampland

evidence.text: Which moduli and charges are admitted when applying the worldsheet unitarity test to six-dimensional supergravity strings and their five-dimensional reductions?

sources.title: Flavor symmetries and automatic enhancement in the 6D supergravity swampland

evidence.text: Which quantum-gravity consistency conditions explain why certain anomaly-free 6d supergravity gauge sectors occur in F-theory only inside larger sectors that cannot be supersymmetrically Higgsed back to the proposed smaller theory?

sources.title: Spectra of BPS strings in 6d supergravity and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can modular bootstrap determine BPS-string elliptic genera, including gauge-instanton strings, in 6d supergravity, and can these spectra test Swampland conjectures in theories lacking F-theory realizations?

sources.title: Enumerating 6D supergravities with T ≤ 1

evidence.text: Can anomaly-free six-dimensional supergravities with at most one tensor multiplet be exhaustively enumerated while allowing arbitrary hypermultiplet representations and numbers of simple gauge factors, and which enumerated models survive additional proposed quantum-gravity bounds?

sources.title: Machine learning the 6d supergravity landscape

evidence.text: Can machine learning on anomaly-coefficient Gram matrices organize six-dimensional supergravity building blocks, identify unusual models, and predict restricted probe-string consistency?

sources.title: The hyperplane string, RCFTs, and the swampland

evidence.text: Can the primitive hyperplane string probe consistency and connectivity of non-geometric, tensor-free 6d quantum gravity theories, particularly where its gauge current algebra nearly saturates the available left-moving central charge?

sources.title: Global anomalies in 6D gauged supergravities

evidence.text: Which locally anomaly-free six-dimensional R-symmetry gauged supergravities also satisfy dyonic-string charge quantisation and globally defined Green–Schwarz counterterm criteria, and what restrictions follow for the total number of vector multiplets?

sources.title: Rational points in the 6d supergravity landscape and simple current extensions

evidence.text: Do five exotic anomaly-free T = 0 six-dimensional supergravity candidates satisfy stronger consistency tests from rational BPS-string worldsheets, and can their refined elliptic genera and global gauge groups be determined?

sources.title: Anomaly-free spectra, unimodular lattices and 6D R-symmetry gauged supergravity

evidence.text: Which six-dimensional N=(1,0) spectra with gauged U(1)R and one tensor multiplet satisfy local anomalies, charge-lattice constraints and the additional global conditions considered, and how restrictive is their arithmetic structure?

sources.title: Anomaly-free six-dimensional $Sp(1)_R$-gauged supergravities

evidence.text: Which six-dimensional Sp(1)_R-gauged supergravity spectra with one tensor multiplet satisfy local anomaly cancellation, string-charge lattice quantization, and positive gauge kinetic terms? How restrictive are these conditions on vector numbers and neutral abelian factors?

sources.title: Reconstructing BPS String Charge Cone in 6d N=(1,0) Supergravity

evidence.text: Can intrinsic six-dimensional EFT data reconstruct the complete closed BPS string charge cone and tensor moduli space, and reveal global consistency obstructions beyond local anomalies and lattice tests?

sources.title: A Systematic search for anomaly-free supergravities in six dimensions

evidence.text: Which six-dimensional chiral N=1 Poincaré and R-symmetry-gauged supergravities satisfy local and global anomaly cancellation, within specified restrictions on tensor content, gauge groups and hypermultiplet representations?

sources.title: A Bound on 6D N=1 supergravities

evidence.text: Use signs of anomaly coefficients to classify factors as type 0, N or P and constrain shared matter. For growing classical rank, use large-rank trace coefficients to restrict representations. Appendix A uses explicit generators, traces and Young-diagram state counting to establish the type-0 positivity ingredient.

sources.title: Global aspects of the space of 6D N = 1 supergravities

evidence.text: Generalized Green–Schwarz–Sagnotti factorization writes I8=(1/2)ΩαβX4αX4β. Anomaly equations determine inner products of a and bi, including a²=9−T and the gravitational condition H−V=273−29T.

sources.title: Anomaly constraints and string/F-theory geometry in 6D quantum gravity

evidence.text: The finiteness argument proceeds by contradiction, separating unbounded numbers of bounded-size simple factors from factors of unbounded dimension. It combines Lorentzian lattice geometry, classification by the sign of b_i², Turán’s theorem and large-rank representation constraints.

sources.title: 6D supergravity without tensor multiplets

evidence.text: Compute group invariants through traces of diagonal generators and Young-tableau states. The Weyl character formula and bounds involving representation dimension and A_R/D_R establish finite b ranges; iterative exclusions sharpen the numerically demanding SU(2) and SU(3) cases.

sources.title: Swampland Bounds on the Abelian Gauge Sector

evidence.text: Turn a bulk counting problem into a finite worldsheet central-charge budget. Establish simultaneous visibility before counting factors; positivity for only a subset bounds only that subset.

sources.title: On the consistency of a class of R-symmetry gauged 6$D$ $\mathcal{N}$=(1,0) supergravities

evidence.text: Evaluate the gauge anomaly bilinear form on cocharacter lattices, distinguishing them from coroot and coweight lattices according to the global gauge group. Combine these tests with imported spin-bordism information.

evidence.text: Can birational geometry produce explicit, uniform upper bounds on the multiplet spectrum of six-dimensional N=(1,0) gravity, beginning with tensor multiplets, and give these bounds a bottom-up interpretation conditional on physical conjectures?

sources.title: Constraint on spinor-vector dualities in six dimensions

evidence.text: What restriction does cancellation of irreducible six-dimensional SO(2N) gauge anomalies impose on spinor–vector dualities, and how is it realized in exact free-fermionic models and smooth heterotic K3 line-bundle spectra?

sources.title: The discrete Green-Schwarz mechanism in 6D F-theory and elliptic genera of non-critical strings

evidence.text: How are global discrete gauge anomalies cancelled in six-dimensional F-theory supergravities, and how can their Green–Schwarz couplings be extracted from non-critical strings and compactification geometry?

sources.title: Charge Lattices and Consistency of 6D Supergravity

evidence.text: Is unimodularity of the allowed dyonic string charge lattice a necessary quantum consistency condition independent of string theory, and which otherwise anomaly-free 6D supergravities does it exclude?

sources.title: Exploring new constraints on Kähler moduli space of 6d $ \mathcal{N} $ = 1 supergravity

evidence.text: Can positivity and boundary consistency of five-dimensional Coulomb branches constrain anomaly-free six-dimensional supergravity beyond anomaly cancellation, particularly by fixing gauge-group global forms and required BPS-string excitations?

sources.title: Exploring 6D origins of 5D supergravities with Chern-Simons terms

evidence.text: Which necessary conditions allow a five-dimensional supergravity with eight or sixteen supercharges, Abelian vectors and ungauged scalars to arise as the low-energy circle reduction of an anomaly-free six-dimensional theory?

sources.title: An infinite swampland of U(1) charge spectra in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: Which massless charge spectra of six-dimensional N = 1 supergravity with one gauged U(1) satisfy known consistency tests, and which can arise in F-theory?

sources.title: Mapping 6D N = 1 supergravities to F-theory

evidence.text: How can anomaly-free chiral six-dimensional supergravity data be mapped systematically to F-theory geometry, and which failures of that map might reveal additional quantum consistency conditions or previously unknown string realizations?

sources.title: (Quadratically) Refined discrete anomaly cancellation

evidence.text: Which nonperturbative Zk gauge anomalies of six-dimensional chiral fermions can a single chiral two-form cancel, and how do quadratic-refinement identities, a specified refinement, and changes of Spin structure restrict the charged spectrum?

sources.title: Generic matter representations in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: Do some hypermultiplet representations require less tuning than others in 6D N=(1,0) supergravity? The comparison fixes the gauged group and discrete anomaly data and measures dimensions of neutral-moduli branches.

sources.title: Finite landscape of 6d N=(1,0) supergravity

evidence.text: Can quantum-gravity consistency conditions beyond anomaly cancellation uniformly bound massless multiplets in 6d N=(1,0) supergravity, without assuming a string or geometric realization?

sources.title: String Defects, Supersymmetry and the Swampland

evidence.text: Which string-defect consistency conditions constrain six-dimensional supergravity beyond anomaly cancellation, and how do explicit orientifolds delimit their applicability to BPS defects, stable non-BPS defects and localized supersymmetry breaking?

sources.title: Anomaly cancellation in six-dimensions

evidence.text: How much K3 topological and spectral information follows from six-dimensional anomaly cancellation, and how does it constrain symmetric and asymmetric orbifolds and enhanced U(1) charges?

sources.title: Fine Tuning, Sequestering, and the Swampland

evidence.text: How does gravity restrict an infinite family of six-dimensional conformal sectors? With supersymmetry-preserving relevant and marginal couplings absent, tensor-branch VEV directions provide the useful parameter count for the ADE (2,0) family.

sources.title: Tensor and vector multiplets in six-dimensional supergravity

evidence.text: How can six-dimensional (1,0) supergravity coupled to n tensor multiplets and vector multiplets be completed to all fermion orders, while its residual gauge and supersymmetry anomalies obey Wess-Zumino consistency conditions?

sources.title: Automatic enhancement in 6D supergravity and F-theory models

evidence.text: When does tuning an anomaly-consistent gauge group and massless matter spectrum in 6D F-theory force a larger gauge symmetry, and can an obstruction to supersymmetric Higgsing explain otherwise apparent swampland spectra?

sources.title: Towards a complete classification of 6D supergravities

evidence.text: How can anomaly cancellation and charge-lattice consistency organize a classification of minimally supersymmetric 6D supergravities across tensor multiplicities, and which sectors obstruct finiteness?

sources.title: String Defects, Supersymmetry and the Swampland

evidence.text: Must the physical string spectrum of a consistent six-dimensional quantum-gravity theory contain a string with null tensor charge?

sources.title: New infinite class of <math display="inline"><mn>6</mn><mi>d</mi></math>, <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> supergravities

evidence.text: Do anomaly cancellation, positivity, charge-lattice unimodularity, and the stated BPS-string anomaly-inflow constraints suffice to reduce six-dimensional supergravity candidates to a finite set, or can infinite families evade all these tests?

sources.title: Anomaly - free supersymmetric models in six-dimensions

evidence.text: Which six-dimensional N=1 spectra satisfy gauge, gravitational, and mixed anomaly cancellation, particularly beyond perturbative heterotic constructions?

sources.title: String Defects, Supersymmetry and the Swampland

evidence.text: Which consistency conditions follow from coupling six-dimensional quantum-gravity theories to string defects when supersymmetry is minimal or broken locally on antibranes?

sources.title: Quantization of anomaly coefficients in 6D $\mathcal{N}=(1,0)$ supergravity

evidence.text: Which additional quantization conditions on 6D N=(1,0) supergravity anomaly coefficients follow from anomaly cancellation and string charge quantization, which require generalized completeness, and how does the global gauge group enter?

sources.title: String Universality in Six Dimensions

evidence.text: Do low-energy consistency conditions characterize the six-dimensional supersymmetric quantum-gravity theories, and does every such consistent theory admit a string compactification? The paper tests this through anomaly constraints, explicit K3 constructions and apparently exceptional infinite families.

sources.title: Quantum gravity on AdS$_{3}$×S$^{3}$ from CFT: bootstrapping n = 21

evidence.text: Can one-loop crossing symmetry and OPE consistency in the dual CFT select n = 21 from the classically arbitrary number of tensor multiplets in six-dimensional (2,0) supergravity on AdS3×S3?

sources.title: New anomaly free supergravities in six dimensions

evidence.text: Which six-dimensional N=(1,0) matter-coupled supergravities cancel local gravitational, gauge and mixed anomalies while admitting positive gauge kinetic terms, and when can their enumeration be complete?

sources.title: An infinite swampland of U(1) charge spectra in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: Do anomaly cancellation and other known consistency conditions bound the massless charge spectra of 6D supergravity with one U(1), and how do these spectra compare with F-theory realizations and Higgsed nonabelian theories?

sources.title: Supergravity anomaly equations from modularity of Calabi--Yau threefolds

evidence.text: Can the local gravitational, gauge and mixed anomaly cancellation conditions of six-dimensional F-theory supergravity be understood geometrically through modular relations between classical intersections and fibral enumerative invariants?

destinations.title: Do Green–Schwarz anomaly cancellation and positivity of kinetic terms alone restrict six-dimensional chiral supergravity with one tensor multiplet to finitely many semisimple gauge groups and matter representations, independently of an explicit UV construction?

How strongly do anomaly cancellation and physical gauge kinetic terms constrain the discrete field content of six-dimensional N=1 supergravity with multiple tensor multiplets, and which additional restrictions characterize F-theory realizations?
How far do anomaly cancellation and physical gauge kinetic terms constrain discrete 6D supergravity data, and can their relation to F-theory geometry establish or obstruct string universality?

Which gauge groups and matter representations satisfy known low-energy consistency conditions for six-dimensional N=1 supergravity without tensor multiplets, focusing on products of SU(N)? Which apparently consistent spectra exceed known string constructions?

Can consistency of strings coupled to tensor fields impose a finite upper bound on independent U(1) gauge factors in six-dimensional N=(1,0) quantum gravity, including theories with non-abelian sectors?
Do three locally anomaly-free, R-symmetry gauged six-dimensional supergravities satisfy stronger quantization and global-anomaly criteria, assuming they possess suitably behaved dyonic strings?

Do anomaly cancellation, string-charge consistency, and BPS-string worldsheet unitarity bound the number of massless modes in six-dimensional supergravity with eight supercharges? Can the same probes constrain bulk matter representations beyond anomaly cancellation?
Which moduli and charges are admitted when applying the worldsheet unitarity test to six-dimensional supergravity strings and their five-dimensional reductions?

Which quantum-gravity consistency conditions explain why certain anomaly-free 6d supergravity gauge sectors occur in F-theory only inside larger sectors that cannot be supersymmetrically Higgsed back to the proposed smaller theory?

Can modular bootstrap determine BPS-string elliptic genera, including gauge-instanton strings, in 6d supergravity, and can these spectra test Swampland conjectures in theories lacking F-theory realizations?

Can anomaly-free six-dimensional supergravities with at most one tensor multiplet be exhaustively enumerated while allowing arbitrary hypermultiplet representations and numbers of simple gauge factors, and which enumerated models survive additional proposed quantum-gravity bounds?
Can machine learning on anomaly-coefficient Gram matrices organize six-dimensional supergravity building blocks, identify unusual models, and predict restricted probe-string consistency?

Can the primitive hyperplane string probe consistency and connectivity of non-geometric, tensor-free 6d quantum gravity theories, particularly where its gauge current algebra nearly saturates the available left-moving central charge?

Which locally anomaly-free six-dimensional R-symmetry gauged supergravities also satisfy dyonic-string charge quantisation and globally defined Green–Schwarz counterterm criteria, and what restrictions follow for the total number of vector multiplets?

Do five exotic anomaly-free T = 0 six-dimensional supergravity candidates satisfy stronger consistency tests from rational BPS-string worldsheets, and can their refined elliptic genera and global gauge groups be determined?

Which six-dimensional N=(1,0) spectra with gauged U(1)R and one tensor multiplet satisfy local anomalies, charge-lattice constraints and the additional global conditions considered, and how restrictive is their arithmetic structure?

Which six-dimensional Sp(1)_R-gauged supergravity spectra with one tensor multiplet satisfy local anomaly cancellation, string-charge lattice quantization, and positive gauge kinetic terms? How restrictive are these conditions on vector numbers and neutral abelian factors?

Can intrinsic six-dimensional EFT data reconstruct the complete closed BPS string charge cone and tensor moduli space, and reveal global consistency obstructions beyond local anomalies and lattice tests?

Which six-dimensional chiral N=1 Poincaré and R-symmetry-gauged supergravities satisfy local and global anomaly cancellation, within specified restrictions on tensor content, gauge groups and hypermultiplet representations?
